name: allocate_pooled_list_node
description: Takes the top node from a free-node stack, whose pointer lives in a global, and inserts it at the front of an active doubly linked list, resetting its link fields and flag byte. It returns without change when the free stack is empty.

name: release_pooled_list_node
description: Unlinks a node from its doubly linked list, joining its neighbours or clearing the list head when it was the only entry, then pushes the node back onto a free-node stack.

name: advance_pseudo_random_state
description: Advances a multi-word state by adding a 32-bit constant read from memory, folding the carry back through rotated bits, and stores the low word of the result in a global counter.

name: set_bitplane_pointers_by_column
description: Derives a row offset from the column position, computes four bitplane addresses spaced one plane apart and writes them into a table, then fills a seven-entry table with a fixed longword. It picks a clipping range by comparing the column against fixed bounds.

name: pack_movement_into_words
description: Combines two signed movement values into a pair of 16-bit words written through the destination pointer, setting the low-order direction bits from sign comparisons and a parity flag held in a global.

name: emit_cached_column_word_pairs
description: Saves the cached entries for the current column, toggles a per-frame slot flag, and writes pairs of words through a callee with a flag bit set on the second word of each pair. Columns outside the visible range write fixed sentinel words and clear the cache.

name: build_blitter_request_for_span
description: Clips a horizontal span against position limits and, when visible, stores a source pointer and a blitter size word computed as rows times 64 plus width into a request record. It then writes four row addresses stepping one plane apart, and calls a callee for any leftover span.

name: emit_clipped_row_blit_request
description: Clips a row range against the column bounds and, when rows remain, writes a size word of rows times 64 plus width, a destination address, and four row addresses stepping one plane apart. A clipped-away span falls back to a callee before the request is written.

name: emit_unclipped_row_blit_request
description: Adds a scaled column offset to the position and, when the vertical span is nonzero, writes a blit size word of span times 64 plus 2, the destination address, and four row addresses stepping one plane apart.

name: emit_blit_request_at_offset
description: When the width delta is nonzero, writes a blit size word from that delta and a destination address, then four row addresses stepping one plane apart. The row multiplier is read from the source record.

name: program_blitter_copy_rows
description: Writes the blitter first and last word masks, modulo values, control registers and source and destination pointers for a four-row copy, then starts each row with a fixed size word.

name: age_linked_list_nodes
description: Resets the list head to empty when it equals a sentinel, then walks the linked list, calls a callee on each node and decrements a per-node byte counter while it is nonzero, until the next-link field is minus one.

name: visit_each_list_node
description: Walks a chain of linked nodes starting from a global head pointer, calling a callee on each node and following the next-link field until it reaches minus one.

name: run_callee_over_record_table
description: Walks a table of fourteen-byte records from a global base, calling a callee on each record until a zero word ends the table. If the base equals a sentinel, the walk starts from the table's first record instead.

name: start_blitter_from_request
description: Copies fields of a request record into blitter registers, including masks, control words, modulo values and pointers, then starts four row blits with a fixed size word while stepping the destination one plane apart.

name: decode_packed_symbol_stream
description: Advances a state machine over a byte-coded stream, consuming counter fields and looking up symbols in fixed tables. When a symbol completes it writes a fixed-size command record through the pointer register, and otherwise resets the pending state.

name: step_back_state_on_failure
description: Clamps a state counter to a fixed value while it is below a threshold. Above the threshold it calls a test routine, and when that routine reports failure it steps the counter back by two and sets the pending-state byte.

name: step_forward_state_on_failure
description: Clamps a state counter to a fixed upper limit when it is at or above the limit. Otherwise it calls a test routine and, on failure, advances the counter by two and sets the pending-state byte to one.

name: lookup_state_code_from_tables
description: Maps the current state byte to an output code by consulting one of several fixed byte tables, choosing the table by state and by the result of a callee. It returns fixed codes for a few special states.

name: poll_cia_fire_button
description: Reads the fire button and disk status bits from CIA port A, tracks press and release transitions in a small state machine, and advances a per-button sequence index through a lookup table when a press is detected.

name: update_linked_node_status
description: Calls a callee eight times in a loop, then decrements a per-node counter byte and, while it stays non-negative, sets a status value of two on the node and on the nodes reached through its link pointers.

name: decrement_node_counter_and_mark
description: Decrements a per-node counter byte and, while it stays non-negative, sets a status value of two on the node and on the nodes reached through its link pointers. A negative counter leaves the links untouched and passes the input value through.

name: mark_chained_nodes_status
description: When a flag byte in the node equals one, sets the status byte of the node linked from it and of that node's successor to two. It always returns zero.

name: check_position_inside_window
description: When the enabled byte is set, compares the two position words of a record against a reference record and, when both differences fall inside a fixed window, marks the record and returns an all-ones byte. Otherwise it returns the input byte unchanged.

name: advance_input_state_on_code
description: Reads a state byte and calls a callee, then either changes the state counter by a column-derived amount or returns a negative status. When the byte at the current pointer matches one of two fixed codes, it sets the state to one and loads a timer value of four.

name: advance_input_state_on_code
description: Reads a state byte and calls a callee, then either changes the state counter by a column-derived amount or returns a negative status. When the byte at the current pointer matches one of two fixed codes, it sets the state to one and loads a timer value of four.

name: set_state_on_matching_code
description: Compares the byte at the pointer against two fixed codes and, on a match, sets the state to one and loads a timer value of four. Otherwise it returns without changing anything.

name: bracket_callee_with_mode_flag
description: Sets a mode flag byte to one when the state equals two, calls a callee, then clears the flag, so the callee runs with the flag visible to it.

name: run_callees_under_mode_flag
description: Sets a mode flag byte from the current state, four for state three and one for state two, calls a callee and a second routine, then clears the flag.

name: run_callees_under_mode_flag
description: Sets a mode flag byte from the current state, four for state three and one for state two, calls a callee and a second routine, then clears the flag.

name: test_grid_cell_occupied
description: Converts two coordinate values into a cell index by shifting each right by four and combining them with a row stride of two hundred, then returns an all-ones value when that cell's entry in a flag table has its low bit set, and zero otherwise.

name: test_flag_table_entry
description: Looks up the byte at the pointer in a flag table and returns an all-ones value when its low bit is set, otherwise it returns the input value unchanged.

name: stub_empty_return
description: Its body is a bare return, so calling it leaves the machine state unchanged.

name: test_value_below_threshold
description: Compares a 16-bit input against a threshold of one hundred and returns an all-ones value when it is below, otherwise it returns the input byte unchanged.

name: program_blitter_single_word_rows
description: Computes a destination address from the position and a byte value, optionally redirects through a callee when a bitmap bit is set, then programs the blitter masks, control words, modulos and pointers and starts four rows of one-word blits.

name: test_cell_neighbours_blocked
description: Reads a cell code and, for the letter X, tests a bitmap bit at an offset derived from the position. For other codes it reads a flag table entry and, when a flag bit is set, checks up to four neighbouring cells through a callee and combines the results into a direction index before returning.

name: store_longword_to_two_tables
description: Stores one longword into two table slots addressed from two base registers, at fixed displacements that are 512 bytes apart.

name: stub_empty_return
description: Its body is a bare return, so calling it leaves the machine state unchanged.

name: stub_empty_return
description: Its body is a bare return, so calling it leaves the machine state unchanged.

name: stub_empty_return
description: Its body is a bare return, so calling it leaves the machine state unchanged.

name: stub_empty_return
description: Its decompiled body is a bare return, so calling it leaves the machine state unchanged.

name: copy_paired_table_into_records
description: Copies two groups of seven rows from a source table into a record array, reading each row's fields and the paired entries 320 bytes further on, and writes them at fixed offsets inside each 164-byte record. A flag byte chooses the destination base.

name: load_scaled_parameters_from_table
description: Reads a longword entry from a table indexed by a byte scaled by eight, then stores it and derived values, scaled by the factors twenty-two, twenty-one and eighteen, into a set of global variables and offsets.

name: wrap_call_passing_registers
description: Calls a single callee and returns the register pair it was given, so the caller sees the register values unchanged.

name: cycle_audio_channel_state
description: Steps a four-state counter that wraps from zero to three. For each state it sets the matching channel flag and stores the input value in that channel's slot, updating a state byte as it goes.

name: program_audio_channel_registers
description: Writes the pointer, length, period and volume registers of one audio channel from per-sample tables, choosing the channel from a pending-channel flag. It then writes a DMA control word that enables that channel.

name: wrap_call_passing_registers
description: Calls a single callee and returns the register pair it was given, so the caller sees the register values unchanged.

name: start_audio_channel_by_index
description: Writes the pointer, length, period and volume registers of the audio channel named by an index argument, using per-sample tables. A pending-channel check decides whether the channel is started now or queued, and the start writes a DMA control word that enables it.

name: tick_audio_channel_countdowns
description: Decrements four countdown counters and, as each reaches zero, sets the matching state value to eight, four, two or one.

name: tick_audio_channel_countdowns
description: Decrements four countdown counters and, as each reaches zero, sets the matching state value to eight, four, two or one.

name: zero_fill_then_walk_records
description: Writes a fixed longword pattern into one block and zero-fills a counted region, then walks a null-terminated table of records. It calls a callee for each record and stores the running address into that record's target pointer.

name: configure_state_specific_parameters
description: Selects one of six per-state parameter sets by a state byte, writing a block of values and pointers for each and calling a callee to reset the region where the state requires it. Any state value outside that set halts in an empty loop.

name: configure_default_state_parameters
description: Writes one fixed parameter block of values and two table-sourced pointers, clears the state flag, and calls a callee to reset the region.

name: copy_nine_records_and_reset
description: Copies nine fixed-size entries from a source table into a destination array with a different stride. It sets a group of word-sized parameters before and after a callee call, changing them between the two states.

name: stub_empty_return
description: Its decompiled body is a bare return, so calling it leaves the machine state unchanged.

name: stub_bad_instruction_data
description: Decoded from an unreached gap that is probably data. Its body adds a constant to the input register and returns, which is not a meaningful routine.

name: wrap_call_passing_registers
description: Calls a single callee and returns the register pair it was given, so the caller sees the register values unchanged.

name: read_disk_track_sectors
description: Writes a sync word and a transfer length to the disk controller, waits for its ready bit, and copies the decoded sector bytes into the destination until the byte count runs out. It then sets the drive control port to all-ones.

name: enable_disk_dma_and_motor
description: Writes the disk sync and transfer registers and sets the DMA control word that enables disk DMA, clears the audio and disk control bits, and sets drive-select and motor bits in the CIA port registers. It then waits through a countdown before clearing the state flag.

name: wait_for_drive_then_reset
description: Sets one drive control bit, polls a CIA status bit while calling a callee on each pass, then writes zero through the pointer and clears the same control bit.

name: zero_word_clear_drive_bit
description: Writes zero through the pointer register and clears one drive control bit in the CIA port byte.

name: pulse_drive_control_and_wait
description: Calls a callee, sets and then clears one drive control bit, clears another, pauses through a countdown, and polls a status bit until it clears.

name: read_disk_track_sectors
description: Syncs to MFM data by writing a sync word and a transfer length, waits on the controller ready bit for each sector, and decodes the bytes into the destination until the byte count runs out. It then sets the drive control port to all-ones.

name: transfer_disk_block_to_memory
description: Writes a buffer pointer and a sync word to the disk controller, starts a fixed-length transfer, waits for it to complete, and copies the decoded bytes into the destination until the count runs out. It then sets the drive control port to all-ones.

name: copy_sectors_from_pointer_list
description: Walks a list of sector source pointers, starting each read on the disk controller with a sync word and transfer register, and copies the decoded bytes into the destination until the byte count runs out. It then sets the drive control port to all-ones.

name: decode_mfm_sector_records
description: Scans for MFM sync words and decodes each sector header to find its sector number, then decodes the data field of 128 long words by recombining odd and even bits. It accumulates a checksum and stops when a sector's checksum is nonzero, storing each valid sector's buffer pointer in a per-sector table.

name: merge_odd_even_bits
description: Combines two longwords from the pointer: the second is masked with a register-held mask, and the first is masked the same way and shifted left by one bit. The two results are ORed to recombine the odd and even bit halves.

name: stub_return_stack_value
description: Returns the value at the top of the stack without any computation, so it passes its input straight through.

name: stub_return_stack_value
description: Returns the value at the top of the stack without any computation, so it passes its input straight through.

name: seek_disk_head_track
description: Clears the step bit in the CIA port and, when the drive needs a reset, polls the track-zero status while stepping the head. It then steps one track at a time toward the requested track, setting a step bit that is cleared again when the low bit of the request is set.

name: latch_drive_select_with_delay
description: Sets bit one of the control byte at the pointer, clears bit zero and sets it again, then pauses through a countdown loop. The input register is returned unchanged.

name: clear_and_latch_drive_bit
description: Clears bit one and then bit zero of the control byte at the pointer, sets bit zero again, and pauses through a countdown loop before returning.

name: fill_region_with_alternating_pattern
description: Fills 7168 words, starting at a fixed offset from the base register, with a word of alternating one and zero bits.

name: step_head_to_target_track
description: Steps a head-position counter one track at a time, choosing the direction by comparing it with the target, until the two match. It then sets a step bit in the control byte at the pointer and clears it again when the low bit of the request is set.

name: stub_empty_return
description: Its decompiled body is a bare return, so calling it leaves the state unchanged. The hardware references listed in its facts do not appear in the code.

name: set_status_after_call
description: Calls a callee, then sets a status byte to all-ones, passing the register value through unchanged.

name: search_name_table_for_match
description: Compares the null-terminated name in the global buffer against each 24-byte entry of a fixed table, returning on a match. When no entry matches within 255 entries it sets a negative status code.

name: validate_table_entry_extent
description: Finds the table entry whose name matches the global buffer, adds its two longword fields, and sets a negative error status when that sum exceeds a fixed limit. A name with no match also sets the error status.

name: set_entry_error_status
description: Sets the shared status word to a fixed negative error value and returns, with no other work.

name: validate_indexed_entry_extent
description: When the index argument is nonzero, takes the entry before it in the 24-byte-stride table, adds its two longword fields, and sets the negative error status when the sum exceeds a fixed limit.

name: stub_empty_return
description: Its decompiled body is a bare return, so calling it leaves the machine state unchanged.

name: copy_and_index_letter_field
description: Copies a 16-byte field from the input pointer into a global buffer, then walks the buffer to its terminating zero byte and maps each uppercase letter to its zero-based alphabet index.

name: copy_blocks_until_count_exhausted
description: Copies bytes from a source table, offset by a block index, into a buffer while decrementing a remaining-count variable, and calls five unnamed routines to set up each block. When the count reaches zero it loops forever if an error flag is set, and otherwise returns.

name: record_unresolved_entry_point
description: The pseudo-code timed out, so the 32-instruction body cannot be read. The facts show only that it is executed in the reference run and entered from outside the static flow, so its behaviour is not recovered here.

name: record_unresolved_entry_point
description: The pseudo-code timed out, so the 16-instruction body cannot be read. The facts show only that it is executed in the reference run and entered from outside the static flow, so its behaviour is not recovered here.

name: invoke_shared_callee_group
description: Forty-seven instructions called from five places and calling three unnamed routines. The pseudo-code timed out, so the purpose of those calls is not recovered.

name: return_constant_minus_one
description: Returns the all-ones 32-bit constant to its caller, with no other action in its two instructions.

name: initialise_working_tables_and_flags
description: Sets a flag from the result of a call and a timing multiplier from two bits of a structure field. It calls unnamed routines with constant arguments to allocate and fill several sized buffers, zeroes blocks of records and words, and ends by calling four unnamed routines. The pseudo-code timed out for this body, so the detail beyond these steps is not recovered.

name: clear_block_and_dispatch_handlers
description: Zeroes a block of several thousand longwords, then calls a handler through one pointer when a flag bit is set and a second handler through a table pointer. It then calls one of two handlers depending on whether the result is zero, or an unnamed routine otherwise.

name: open_narrator_device_port
description: Creates a port with a size argument of seventy, then opens the device named in the text through a second call. It returns one when both steps succeed and zero when either fails, releasing the port on failure.

name: close_narrator_device_port
description: If the open flag is set, it checks a pending request and closes the device through a library call. It then releases the two handles held in the state block when they are non-null.

name: stub_empty_return
description: Its decompiled body is a bare return, so calling it leaves the machine state unchanged.

name: configure_channel_block_fields
description: Writes a longword from one structure into a field of a second structure, clears a word, and sets another word to a fixed control value. It calls two unnamed routines around those writes.

name: poll_marker_byte_sequence
description: Calls a routine and loops while its result is below one. Whenever the byte at a global pointer equals the character three, it busy-waits on that byte, runs a sequence of calls, and waits again, then returns the final result.

name: forward_two_argument_call
description: Forwards its two arguments unchanged to one unnamed routine and returns.

name: read_input_flags
description: Returns a byte built from two bits of a global variable: one when bit six is clear, plus two when bit two is clear. The register names in its facts do not appear in the code.

name: set_state_byte_constant
description: Stores a fixed byte value into a global variable and returns. The interrupt-enable register named in its facts is not written in the code.

name: advance_feedback_state_modulo
description: Advances a 32-bit state held in a global by shifting it left and folding in a fixed feedback constant when the carry is set. For a positive argument it returns the quotient and remainder of the state divided by that argument, packed into one result; for a non-positive argument it stores the negated argument as the state.

name: rotate_complement_and_delay
description: When a flag bit is set, returns the complement of a state byte rotated right by one bit, waits through a countdown, and clears a second flag bit. The serial and interrupt registers named in its facts are not visible in the code.

name: build_bitplane_pointer_pairs
description: Copies a block of 180 words from a fixed table into a buffer, then writes high and low word pairs for four addresses spaced 8000 bytes apart, masking each high word to six bits. It also writes pairs for eight further entries taken from a second pointer.

name: set_control_block_fixed_words
description: Writes thirteen fixed words into a control structure at several offsets, then calls two unnamed routines.

name: configure_control_block_with_param
description: Calls two unnamed routines, writes a fixed word and the input longword into a control structure, writes a second fixed word, and then calls one unnamed routine.

name: return_stored_longword
description: Returns the longword stored at a fixed negative offset from the base register, without changing anything.

name: update_bitplane_pointer_pairs
description: Stores the first argument in a state longword unless it is the sentinel value. When the second argument is not the sentinel, it writes high and low word pairs for four addresses spaced 8000 bytes apart, masking each high word to six bits. The facts also list a raster-line wait called from this routine.

name: copy_sixteen_words_into_block
description: Copies sixteen words from the input pointer into alternate word slots of a structure block, starting at a fixed offset from the base.

name: stub_empty_return
description: Its decompiled body is a bare return, so calling it leaves the machine state unchanged.

name: stub_empty_return
description: Its decompiled body is a bare return, so calling it leaves the machine state unchanged.

name: invoke_three_unnamed_calls
description: Calls one unnamed routine with an offset from a register, a second with all-ones arguments, and a third with no arguments, then returns.

name: chain_three_calls_with_local
description: Passes its first argument and the address of a local longword to one unnamed routine, calls another with a fixed constant and that longword, and calls a third with the result.

name: read_next_byte_from_cursor
description: Reads the byte at the offset held in a cursor word, advances the cursor by one, and returns that byte.

name: load_vol_cnf_entries
description: Clears a table of twenty 20-byte entries, then opens the file named by the text VOL.CNF through a call. When the open succeeds it reads a count and that many 20-byte entries, each with a four-byte value, into the table, then closes the handle.

name: read_value_under_handle
description: Calls an unnamed routine with a minus-two argument. When that returns a non-zero handle, it calls two routines with the handle and a stored structure field, then returns a longword taken from the structure; otherwise it returns zero.

name: read_word_under_handle
description: Calls an unnamed routine with a minus-two argument. When that returns a non-zero handle, it calls two routines with the handle and a stored structure field, then returns the low word of a longword taken from the structure. The text DH0: is referenced in the facts.

name: read_word_under_handle
description: Calls an unnamed routine with a minus-two argument. When that returns a non-zero handle, it calls two routines with the handle and a stored structure field, then returns the low word of a longword taken from the structure.

name: invoke_two_unnamed_calls
description: Forty-three instructions called from one place that call two unnamed routines. The pseudo-code timed out, so the purpose of those calls is not recovered.

name: forward_single_unnamed_call
description: Twenty-four instructions, entered through an address-of reference, that call one unnamed routine. The pseudo-code timed out, so this is recorded as a call forwarder.

name: setup_data_files_and_tables
description: A 293-instruction routine that references the file names AUTO00.PRC, poldat.dat and texte.dat and the graphics and translator library names. It sets a flag from a call result, scales a timing value from a structure field, allocates and clears working tables of fixed sizes, waits for a raster line, and calls eleven unnamed routines. The facts do not show which file each call touches.

name: reset_state_marker_fields
description: Clears a longword field and sets a word field to all-ones in the state block, with no other effect.

name: visit_list_nodes_with_code
description: Walks a singly linked list from a state pointer, following the first longword of each node, and calls a callee with each node and the fixed code value 214. It then calls one more unnamed routine.

name: flush_pending_slot_request
description: When the pending index at a fixed offset is non-negative, calls three unnamed routines with that index, two stored values and a buffer address, then resets the pending index to minus one.

name: fill_buffer_and_find_entry
description: Returns minus one when no request is pending. Otherwise it fills the buffer at the argument with bytes from an unnamed reader until a count check fails, then tests table entries with a callee and returns the index of the first match, or minus one when none matches.

name: find_entry_with_failing_block
description: Scans the table, skipping entries whose id equals the argument. For each remaining entry it calls a routine on successive 13-byte records, and returns the index of the first entry where one of those calls fails, or minus one.

name: find_failing_block_for_id
description: Like its neighbour, but it tests only entries whose id equals the argument. It calls a routine on successive 13-byte records and returns the index of the first entry where one call fails, or minus one when none does.

name: lookup_slot_with_retry
description: Looks up a slot for the argument and, when the first lookup fails, retries through a second lookup. When a slot is found it calls a routine on that slot's record, and returns the lookup result, or minus one when every attempt fails.

name: read_block_with_product_length
description: Opens a handle with a fixed code, reads two 16-bit values from it, and passes a buffer to an unnamed routine with a length equal to their product. It then closes the handle.

name: depack_bit_stream_backwards
description: Unpacks a bit-coded stream from its end toward its start. For each step it reads a flag bit: when the flag is set it copies a run of earlier output bytes, and otherwise it reads literal bits through the bit reader and writes them. It stops when the output pointer reaches the input start and calls the bit reader's refill routine as needed.

name: depack_stream_alternate_entry
description: An alternate entry into the bit-stream depacking loop. It reads a short count, then copies earlier output bytes or decodes literal bits in the same way as the main depacker, and is reached from one place.

name: depack_copy_run_entry
description: Another entry into the depacking loop that starts with a bit-reader call. It copies earlier output bytes for a back-reference and otherwise decodes literal bits, sharing the loop with the main depacker.

name: depack_literal_entry_point
description: A further entry into the depacking loop that reads a bit-reader count and then writes literal bytes or copies a back-reference run, sharing the loop with the main depacker.

name: fill_global_word_countdown
description: Writes successive word values, counting down from all-ones to one, into a global word and then returns. The color register named in its facts is not written in the code.

name: stub_empty_return
description: Its decompiled body is a bare return, so calling it leaves the machine state unchanged.

name: release_pending_entries_then_check
description: Walks fifty fixed records, calling a callee on each non-null pointer with its stored word and then clearing that pointer and word. It then calls one unnamed routine and returns; the code after that point is decoded from data.

name: show_insert_disk_prompt
description: Builds a disk-insert prompt in stack buffers from the text Please insert DISK, VOL. and into drive, taking the volume name from a stored slot. It draws each line through unnamed routines and draws one further line when the parameter is minus two.

name: idle_loop_after_wait
description: Calls a routine until a stack-held word becomes zero, then loops forever calling a second routine after a third. It is called from the boot entry.

name: prepare_display_planes
description: Calls several routines to set up the display, computes two plane addresses 32000 bytes past the stored base pointers, and calls graphics routines with those addresses and a height of 200 before returning. It is called from the boot entry and one more place.

name: render_message_box_text
description: Lays out a message whose lines are separated by vertical bars: it finds the longest line, computes the box width and centre offset, and draws the box. It then draws each line glyph by glyph, using per-character width and glyph-index tables and wrapping at spaces.

name: draw_message_text_lines
description: Continuation of the message renderer: it draws each line glyph by glyph using the character width and glyph-index tables, advancing word-wrapped positions until the text ends.

name: draw_message_box_lines
description: A second entry into the message text drawing loop, reached after the box width is computed. It draws each line glyph by glyph until the text ends, with word-wrapped positions.

name: draw_message_box_frame
description: Entry into the message renderer that computes the box width from a count multiplied by seven plus twenty, clamps it between 180 and 300, and draws the box and its text lines. It then draws the frame edges with a line routine.

name: draw_message_text_step
description: Fragment of the message renderer that advances the text pointer by a step count, then measures and draws each word glyph by glyph using the character width and glyph-index tables, until the text ends.

name: draw_message_line_loop
description: Loop of the message renderer that draws the glyphs of each line. When the text ends it computes a centred horizontal offset for the final line and draws it.

name: draw_message_glyph_run
description: Draws a run of glyphs for the current character value, advancing the horizontal position by the word gap on spaces and ending a line when the text is exhausted.

name: draw_message_screen_frame
description: A 312-instruction part of the message renderer that draws glyphs line by line, centres the lines within the box, and draws the frame lines. It also calls a graphics library stub at a fixed offset and four unnamed routines.

name: read_text_entry_line
description: Reads keys until Return or Escape ends the entry. It accepts letters, digits and spaces into a buffer of up to nineteen characters, erases the last character on backspace, draws each glyph, and draws a cursor block. The keys come from a library call.

name: read_text_entry_key_loop
description: Second entry into the text entry loop, for a key already read. It accepts or rejects characters, handles backspace, redraws the cursor, and polls for further keys until Return or Escape.

name: process_text_entry_key
description: Processes one key of the text entry: backspace removes the last character, printable letters, digits and spaces are appended within the buffer limit, and the cursor is redrawn before the next key is polled.

name: call_pair_with_library_stub
description: Five instructions that call a library stub at a fixed offset and two unnamed routines.

name: switch_table_row_with_deltas
description: When the requested index differs from the current one, it accumulates the position differences between the old and new table rows, copies sixteen words from the new row into a list, zeroes two trailing words, calls an unnamed routine, and stores the new index.

name: copy_length_prefixed_string
description: Copies a length-prefixed string: it reads the count byte at the source address, copies that many following bytes to the destination, and writes a terminating zero byte. The hint for this routine described a null-terminated copy, which the code does not match.

name: scan_entries_until_failure
description: Walks a linked list from a pointer in the state block. For each entry whose flag word is zero it calls two routines and tests the result of the second, and the first failure stops the walk. It returns the final entry pointer combined with the failure flag.

name: find_trackdisk_device_status
description: Calls the exec FindName function, indexes a table of device pointers by the argument, and returns a status built from bytes at fixed offsets of the chosen device, combined with the input register. Its text references the trackdisk.device name.

name: poll_status_with_retry_limit
description: Polls a status routine and counts failures, returning minus one once the count passes one hundred. Otherwise it calls an unnamed routine with a fixed tag and returns zero, or minus one when that call fails.

name: examine_file_size_by_lock
description: Allocates a 512-byte block, locks the named path through the DOS lock wrapper, and examines it into the block. It stores the longword at offset 124 of the block into the caller's output, then unlocks and frees the block; any failure returns minus one.

name: allocate_tagged_record
description: Allocates a record sized from a stored count and initialises its fields, writes the four-character tag MANX into it, and fills a list entry from a lookup. One of two branches is taken depending on the first argument, then an unnamed library routine is called.

name: match_name_and_launch_task
description: Looks up the current task record and, when it holds a tracked entry, allocates a request block with the tag word. It compares the requested name with the stored name byte by byte, then calls unnamed routines to set up the launch and returns a status code.

name: create_dos_process_from_lock
description: Looks up the current task record and, when it holds a tracked entry, compares names byte by byte, duplicates a lock through the DOS wrapper, and creates a process through the CreateProc library stub using a stored name and entry pointer. It calls eleven unnamed routines along the way.

name: record_unresolved_called_body
description: The decompiled body shows only a bare return, which does not match the 113-instruction count in the facts. The library stub and two unnamed calls listed in the facts cannot be confirmed, so no behaviour is recovered.

name: copy_string_to_buffer
description: Copies bytes from a source string into the destination until a zero byte is copied, including that terminator. It returns the original destination pointer.

name: copy_string_to_buffer
description: Copies bytes from a source string into the destination until a zero byte is copied, including that terminator. It returns the original destination pointer.
